targetAudience.primary: Platform architects governing workspace-controlled agent capabilities
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands configuration layering, workspace trust and tool materialization.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A trust result can remain decorative while untrusted configuration still creates executable capabilities.

whyNow: A same-day merged Gemini CLI change gives restrictive trust signals precedence, maps unresolved trust to false, fails on malformed trust configuration, and removes demonstrated workspace-controlled capability settings from effective configuration.

externalHook.description: Workspace trust changes the configuration that is allowed to materialize tools, policies and related capabilities.

coreProposition: Workspace trust becomes an enforceable authority boundary only when its result shapes capability admission: negative or unresolved trust should reduce the effective executable surface before materialization, while revoking capability instances that already exist remains a separate lifecycle responsibility.

originalValue.description: Treats trust as a capability-admission transform rather than a status label, while separating admission-time filtering from live revocation.

readerTakeaway: Compute the effective capability surface from trust before materialization, fail closed on unresolved authority, and design a separate reconciliation mechanism for already-created capabilities.

supported: Restrictive trust signals take precedence and unresolved trust becomes false in the demonstrated implementation.
Malformed trust configuration fails rather than silently broadening authority.
Named workspace-controlled MCP, policy, tool and telemetry settings are removed from effective configuration when untrusted.
uncertain: How active capability instances should be reconciled after trust changes
Which observation capabilities require separate governance

firstPartyRole.rationale: The conclusion is a general workspace-trust and capability-admission pattern.

decisionReason: The source change supports a concrete fail-closed admission mechanism and a bounded distinction between configuration filtering and lifecycle revocation.
